_meta.task: DEEP XCOM (EU2012 + XCOM2/WOTC) research for Void Skirmish 3D tactics clone - gaps pass
_meta.purpose: Hard-number, implementable answers to 6 gaps: enemy COUNT per mission, map SIZE (tiles), full enemy ROSTER with stats, AI behavior, campaign progression, difficulty knobs. Every number is from a cited source. Firaxis canonical stat tables (UFOpaedia infoboxes, GDC talk) are unflagged; community-measured figures (Steam/GameFAQs threads, fan datamine blogs) are explicitly flagged 'community-measured'.
_meta.abbrev: EU = XCOM: Enemy Unknown/Within (2012); X2 = XCOM 2 / War of the Chosen (2016). WOTC = War of the Chosen expansion.

stat_difficulty_format.EU: All EU stat strings are Easy/Normal/Classic/Impossible (4 values). Single value = same on all difficulties.
stat_difficulty_format.X2: All X2 stat strings are Rookie/Veteran/Commander/Legend (4 values). UFOpaedia infobox numbers are the source; Commander (3rd value) is the canonical 'standard' difficulty.

movement_tile_conversion.EU: tiles_blue = floor(mobility * 0.666); dash = floor(mobility * 0.666 * 2). Mobility 12 = 7 tiles blue / 15 dash (straight line); diagonals are cheaper (12 mob = 5 diag-tiles blue). Source: ufopaedia Movement_(EU2012).
movement_tile_conversion.X2: tiles_blue = mobility / 1.5; dash = blue * 2. Mobility 12 = 8 blue / 16 dash; 14 = 9; 15 = 10; 16 = 11; 18 = 12. Source: ufopaedia + Fandom Mobility + Steam consensus.
movement_tile_conversion.clone_note: Void Skirmish's content.json stores enemy.movement as TILES (e.g. 4) and aim as 0-1 (e.g. 0.66). The enemy_roster below gives native XCOM stats PLUS a 'movement_tiles' field already converted to blue-move tiles for direct use. Aim 0-100 -> divide by 100 for the 0-1 field.

_meta.fetch_note: ufopaedia.org scraped via Python urllib (canonical infoboxes; WebFetch 403s it). Fandom + StrategyWiki 403 BOTH WebFetch and urllib - their numbers came via WebSearch summaries (community-measured / secondary). GDC 2018 Plot-and-Parcel PDF downloaded and text-extracted directly (Firaxis primary source). vigaroe.com (detailed fan datamine) is DNS-unreachable from this box; its figures arrived only via WebSearch snippets and are flagged.

enemy_count_per_mission.headline: XCOM fields MORE aliens than the squad on every mission past the tutorial. Squad is 4 (EU early) to 6 (EU/X2 max). Aliens: 6-10 early, 12-18 mid/terror, 18-28 late/UFO/base. Aliens come in PODS of 1-3 (EU) or 2-3 (X2); only ~1 pod is active/visible at a time, which is why on-screen it can FEEL like only 3-5 enemies even when the map holds 12+. The clone must (a) raise totals and (b) deliver them as pods that reveal over the mission.

squad_size.EU: Starts at 4 deployable soldiers; upgradable to 5 then 6 (Officer Training School: Squad Size I and II). 6 is the campaign max.
squad_size.X2: Starts at 4; upgradable to 5 then 6 via Guerrilla Tactics School. 6 is standard max (mods/WOTC can reach more).
squad_size.clone_recommendation: Keep squad at 5 (the current Void Skirmish value). Enemy totals below are tuned against a 5-soldier squad.

EU2012_CANONICAL.source: ufopaedia.org Alien_Deployment_(EU2012) - Firaxis-datamined Mission Deployment tables. CANONICAL (not community-measured). Format per cell: pods x (avg pod size) = total aliens. Difficulty columns Easy/Normal/Classic/Impossible.
EU2012_CANONICAL.pod_size_rule: Each pod 1-3 aliens. Soldier pods = one species. Secondary pods (terror/UFO) = 1 main + 1-2 escorts of another species. Pods of 3 are the norm at higher difficulty; pods of 2 common on Easy/Normal and for special units (Sectopod, Mechtoid).

abductions.note: Abductions = Soldier pods only. Each mission gets a randomly-rolled difficulty rating shown on the selection screen.

terror_sites.note: Terror = Secondary pods only, always rated Very Difficult. Civilians die each enemy turn. Can field up to 5 Cyberdiscs (or 5 Sectopods on Impossible).

council_missions.note: Soldier pods + DYNAMIC aliens that drop from the sky mid-mission (usually Thin Men). Asset-recovery variant has no dynamic drops. Totals ramp by month.

ufo_missions.note: UFOs add a COMMANDER pod (1-3, on the bridge) plus Soldier pods, plus Secondary pods on Abductor-size and up. Landed UFOs field MORE than crashed (crash kills some aliens). Numbers below are total aliens (Normal/Classic ~ same; Impossible higher).

EU2012_CANONICAL.concrete_summary: EARLY abduction = 2-3 pods x 3 = 6-9 aliens. MID terror/council = 4-5 pods = 10-16. LATE UFO/base = 7-11 pods = 18-28 aliens. The squad is 4-6. So aliens outnumber the squad ~1.5x early to ~4-5x late.

XCOM2_VANILLA.source_quality: community-measured (Steam consensus threads + Fandom Game_difficulty summary). X2 has NO single published Firaxis deployment table like EU; numbers are datamined/measured by the community and vary with Force Level + region strength.
XCOM2_VANILLA.counting_caveat: The pre-mission enemy-count display ONLY counts aliens in pods present at mission START. It EXCLUDES: telegraphed reinforcement drops, hidden Faceless on Retaliation, the Lost waves, turrets, and Chosen. Actual total fought is higher.
XCOM2_VANILLA.pods: 2-3 enemies each. Veteran = mostly 2/pod. Commander/Legend = mostly 3/pod (early pods can still be 2; Gatecrasher tutorial always has one 2-pod).

total_enemies_by_mission_rating_commande.note: These are starting-pod aliens on Commander. Add 2-4 from a typical reinforcement drop. Retaliation adds 1-3 Faceless. Lost-infested maps add endless weak Lost waves on top.

pods_per_mission_disputed.value: Easy 2-4 pods, Moderate 5-6, Difficult 7-8, Very Difficult 8-10
pods_per_mission_disputed.flag: DISPUTED / likely Long-War-inflated. This pod-count source conflicts with the enemy-TOTAL source above (5-6 pods of 2-3 would be 10-18, not 8). Trust the enemy-TOTAL row (6/8/9/11) for VANILLA; the high pod counts describe Long War 2 or heavily-modded play.

long_war_2_reference.note: LW2 (the big overhaul) is where the huge counts come from: activity-level bands extremely-light 7-9, very-light 10-12, light 13-15, light-moderate 16-18, moderate 19-21, moderate-heavy 22-24, heavy 25-27, very-heavy 28-30, extremely-heavy 31-34. Force Level 1-20. NOT vanilla - use only if you want LW-scale swarms.
long_war_2_reference.source_quality: canonical for the LW2 MOD, not base XCOM 2

clone_recommendation.principle: Owner wants MORE bad guys than the squad. XCOM agrees: never field fewer aliens than soldiers outside a tutorial. Deliver counts as PODS so the screen reveals them gradually (XCOM's signature pacing) instead of dumping all at once.
clone_recommendation.vs_current_build: Current Void Skirmish (content.json) already ramps 9->18 enemies vs a 5-squad across 7 missions on 36x44 -> 48x56 grids. That LOW end (9) is fine but feels thin because there is no pod system (all 9 sit visible/aggressive at once = either trivial or overwhelming, never the XCOM reveal cadence). FIX = (1) bump totals to 8 -> 22, (2) GROUP into pods of 2-3 with dormant-until-LOS activation, (3) enlarge maps (see map_dimensions).
clone_recommendation.pod_sizing_formula: enemies_total for mission i; pods = ceil(enemies_total / 3); assign 3 per pod, last pod gets the remainder (min 2). Place each pod as a cluster with a patrol anchor; keep dormant until a soldier gains LOS. On reveal, scatter to cover (see enemy_ai_behavior.activation).
clone_recommendation.recommended_totals_vs_squad5: M1:8, M2:10, M3:12, M4:14, M5:16, M6:18, M7:22 (see campaign_ramp for full pod layout). Aliens always >= squad; ratio climbs from 1.6x to 4.4x.

map_dimensions.headline: EU maps are 40-60 tiles per side, 2 or 4 height levels. X2 maps are assembled from parcels (12x12 / 12x24 / 24x24 tiles) dropped into hand-authored plots; a full plot is roughly 60-90+ tiles per side. A soldier crosses ~7-8 tiles on a single move and ~15-16 on a dash, so an XCOM map takes 4-8 dashes (8-15 turns) to cross end-to-end - that traversal time is WHY XCOM missions 'take a while'. For the clone the owner wants LARGE: push to 56-72 tiles per side.

EU2012.height_levels: 2 or 4 vertical levels on most maps.
EU2012.abduction_typical: 6,000-12,000 floor tiles (height ignored) -> roughly 55x55 to 70x70 bounding box if square, but playable footprint per level is ~40-55 per side (rest is height/blocked). source_quality: community-measured
EU2012.ufo_crash_landing: 15,000-20,000 floor tiles (the big open wilderness approach + UFO interior).
EU2012.map_pool: ~68 base maps + ~30 Enemy Within + 3 Slingshot DLC = ~115 total, ~82 unique (per ufopaedia Maps_(EU2012), canonical).
EU2012.source_quality: tile dimensions are community-measured (Firaxis never published them); map COUNTS are canonical.

XCOM2_plot_parcel.source: GDC 2018 'Plot and Parcel: Procedural Level Design in XCOM 2', Brian Hess (Lead Level Designer, Firaxis). PRIMARY/CANONICAL - extracted directly from the talk PDF.

parcel_tile_sizes.note: Verbatim from the GDC slide 'Initial Parcel Rules'. Parcels have a random facing and randomly-drawn building content each load.

XCOM2_plot_parcel.plot: The hand-authored master layout (roads/rivers/paths = 'Plot Cover Parcels'/PCPs) with empty slots sized for each parcel bucket. A plot is filled by random parcel draws + objective + patrol routes at load time.
XCOM2_plot_parcel.shipped_content: XCOM 2 shipped with 80 plots, 200+ parcels, 450+ PCPs (canonical, GDC slide 'Taking Stock').
XCOM2_plot_parcel.effective_map_size: A plot holding e.g. a couple of 24x24 large parcels + 12x24 mediums + road PCPs lands roughly 60-90 tiles per side overall. Firaxis did NOT publish a single official per-map tile dimension in the talk; the parcel sizes are the hard numbers. (effective per-side estimate = derived, flagged.)

soldier_traversal.single_move_tiles: EU mobility-12 soldier = 7 tiles (blue). X2 mobility-12 = 8 tiles (blue).
soldier_traversal.dash_tiles: EU = 15 tiles; X2 = 16 tiles (both actions on movement).
soldier_traversal.turns_to_cross_a_50_tile_map: ~50 / 15 = ~3-4 dashes one-way if running straight and unopposed. Real missions = 8-15 player turns because you move in cover-to-cover hops (single moves, overwatch, fights), not continuous dashes. THIS is the 'XCOM takes a while' feel: the map is ~6-8 dashes deep, but you only safely advance 1 cover bound per turn.
soldier_traversal.source: ufopaedia Movement_(EU2012) (canonical EU); Fandom Mobility + Steam consensus (X2, community-measured).

clone_recommendation.principle: Owner wants LARGE. The current 36x44 is BELOW XCOM's floor (40). Move to the upper half of XCOM's range and scale per mission so late maps feel like a campaign escalation.
clone_recommendation.rationale: 48 = XCOM's small-but-real abduction; 60 = XCOM base-defense size; 72 = pushing toward a large UFO approach. All within the canonical 40-72 envelope, none cartoonishly large for a browser engine. Pair with single-move = 6-7 tiles and dash = 12-14 tiles (your enemy.movement of 4-6 tiles is on the low side; bump player blue-move to ~6 so a 60-tile map is ~5 dashes deep, matching XCOM's 8-12 turn pacing).
clone_recommendation.construction: Assemble each map from authored 'parcel' chunks (cover clusters + a building or two) snapped onto tile anchors, with open road/plaza connective tissue between - exactly the plot+parcel recipe. Scatter low/high cover only at anchor points so the grid stays readable. Place pods along patrol anchors spread across the map so traversal naturally reveals them one at a time.
clone_recommendation.performance_note: 72x72 = 5,184 ground tiles single-level. Fine for the 3D engine IF you follow existing ForgeFlow FPS rules: instanced tile/cover meshes, strip GLB-embedded lights, DPR cap ~1.5, shadow map ~1024, frustum-cull off-camera parcels.

enemy_roster.name: Sectoid
enemy_roster.signature: Mind Merge (link to another Sectoid: linked unit gets +1HP/+25Will/+25crit; if merge-caster dies, linked unit dies). Early-game psi fodder; dies to one good hit.

enemy_roster.name: Sectoid Commander
enemy_roster.signature: Mind Control an XCOM soldier; Psi Panic; Mindfray (-Will). UFO commander pod after the alien base falls.

enemy_roster.name: Thin Man
enemy_roster.signature: Leaps walls/rooftops; Poison Spit (AoE cloud, -aim/-mobility DoT); leaves a poison cloud on death. Council-mission staple + dynamic sky-drop.

enemy_roster.name: Floater
enemy_roster.signature: Flight: can launch to any tile/high ground (costs the turn) for height aim+def. Low base aim. Has 35 fuel.

enemy_roster.name: Heavy Floater
enemy_roster.signature: Upgraded Floater; flight + Bombard (long-range grenade launch). Mid-game flyer.

enemy_roster.name: Muton
enemy_roster.signature: Tanky line infantry; throws Alien Grenades; Intimidate (panic on wound). Weak to psi. The mid-game workhorse.

enemy_roster.name: Muton Elite
enemy_roster.signature: Late-game Muton; high aim, +20-30 defense, heavy plasma. Escorts Ethereals.

enemy_roster.name: Berserker
enemy_roster.signature: Bull Rush: charges in a straight line THROUGH cover for a heavy melee hit. Bloodlust: charges whoever wounds it. Hardened (-60% incoming crit). High HP melee bruiser.

enemy_roster.name: Cyberdisc
enemy_roster.signature: Robotic saucer; closed<->open assault form; Death Blossom (close-range AoE); Flight + Evasion (-20 aim vs it airborne); escorts Drones. Hardened.

enemy_roster.name: Drone
enemy_roster.signature: Small flying robot; repairs Cyberdiscs/Sectopods; weak beam. Robotic (immune to psi/poison/stun).

enemy_roster.name: Chryssalid
enemy_roster.damage: high melee + poison (EU2012 publishes no clean base-damage range; the hit is effectively lethal via crit and ALWAYS poisons)
enemy_roster.signature: Fastest unit in EU (13 tiles blue / 26 dash). Melee hit poisons; a killed civilian/soldier becomes a ZOMBIE that hatches a NEW Chryssalid in ~3 turns. Terror-mission nightmare. damage_flag: community/qualitative - no canonical numeric range in EU stat table.

enemy_roster.name: Zombie
enemy_roster.signature: Spawned when a Chryssalid kills an organic. Slow shambler; if not killed within ~3 turns it births a Chryssalid. Kill it fast to deny the spawn. hp_flag: approximate, not a clean published table value.

enemy_roster.name: Sectopod
enemy_roster.signature: Huge armored robot. Cannon Fire = AoE line damage; Cluster Bomb = telegraphed area barrage next turn. Hardened + Reinforced Armor (EW: -50% all damage). Robotic. Top-tier.

enemy_roster.name: Ethereal
enemy_roster.damage: psi (Rift/Mindfray scale with target Will, not a fixed range)
enemy_roster.signature: Top psi: Mind Control, Psi Panic, Rift (wide AoE psi, devastating vs low-Will/robotic), Reflect. Will 120-155. Final-boss tier (Uber Ethereal on the Temple Ship). damage_flag: will-scaled, no fixed base-damage number.

enemy_roster.name: Outsider
enemy_roster.signature: Crystalline UFO guardian (commander pod on Scouts early game). Shatters into a shard on death (research item). Appears from game start.

enemy_roster.name: Mechtoid
enemy_roster.signature: Enemy Within DLC. Sectoid-piloted mech; twin plasma volley; gains a 6HP 50%-damage-reduction shield if a Sectoid Mind Merges with it (kill the Sectoid to drop the shield). Robotic.

enemy_roster.name: ADVENT Trooper
enemy_roster.signature: Basic grunt, the bread-and-butter pod follower. No special ability. Takes cover, shoots, overwatches.

enemy_roster.name: ADVENT Officer
enemy_roster.signature: Mark Target (all nearby Troopers focus-fire the marked soldier); Command Aura buffs allies; can summon reinforcements. Pod leader. Dodge 15, crit 10 (Cmd/Legend).

enemy_roster.name: ADVENT Stun Lancer
enemy_roster.signature: RUSHES into melee with a stun baton (stuns/dazes a soldier = skip their next turn). Suicidally aggressive; closes distance every turn. Fast (9 tiles).

enemy_roster.name: ADVENT Shieldbearer
enemy_roster.signature: Energy Shield: grants nearby allies a temporary HP shield (absorbs damage before HP). Priority kill - neutralizes a whole pod's effective HP. Tanky.

enemy_roster.name: ADVENT MEC
enemy_roster.signature: Robotic mech (2 armor approx). Micro-missiles = AoE. Hackable (Specialist can stun/control). High HP + armor. Robotic. armor_flag: ~2, prose-stated not in infobox.

enemy_roster.name: ADVENT Turret
enemy_roster.signature: STATIONARY rooftop/checkpoint gun. Armor 1/2/3/3. Cannot move; only fires at LOS targets. Hackable. NOT counted in pre-mission enemy total. source_quality: community-measured (vigaroe via search).

enemy_roster.name: Sectoid
enemy_roster.signature: Bigger psionic Sectoid. Mindspin (random Disorient/Panic/Mind Control). Psi Reanimate (raise a corpse as a Psi-Zombie). Takes DOUBLE damage from melee. Kill it to free its thralls. Will 80-100.

enemy_roster.name: Viper
enemy_roster.signature: Tongue Pull (yank a soldier out of cover toward the Viper) + Bind (coil/immobilize + DoT until allies kill the Viper or free them) + Poison Spit AoE. High Dodge (15/25/33). The signature X2 control enemy.

enemy_roster.name: Muton
enemy_roster.signature: Tank line infantry. Suppression (-aim pin + reaction fire). COUNTERATTACK: high chance to negate a melee attack and counter-stab. Throws grenades at clustered squads. The X2 mid-game wall.

enemy_roster.name: Archon
enemy_roster.signature: Flying angel (Dodge 25). Blazing Pinions: flies up and marks tiles, raining AoE rockets NEXT turn (telegraphed, like Cluster Bomb). Battle Frenzy: when wounded, gains +1 action for 2 turns and melees. High-mobility flyer.

enemy_roster.name: Andromedon
enemy_roster.signature: TWO-STAGE tank. Living form has 4 armor (3 on Rookie) + acid attacks that leave damaging pools. When the body dies, a robotic ANDROMEDON SHELL stands up (HP 14/14/18/21, 0 armor, melee 7-10) and keeps fighting = second health bar. Acid SHREDS armor.

enemy_roster.name: Gatekeeper
enemy_roster.signature: Floating armored sphere. Opens to fire a heavy beam; closes = high defense (25-40) + armor. Gateway/Consume can REANIMATE nearby corpses into Psi-Zombies and heal itself. Dying Explosion on death. Late-game heavy. Will 100-120.

enemy_roster.name: Codex
enemy_roster.signature: TELEPORTS instead of walking (no-cooldown blink). Psionic Rift: marks a large area that DISABLES primary weapons inside it, then detonates next turn for damage. CLONE: every time it takes damage it splits into two, each with HALF the remaining HP. Hard to pin down. source_quality: stats community-measured (vigaroe/Fandom via search).

enemy_roster.name: Faceless
enemy_roster.signature: DISGUISED as a civilian on Retaliation maps; transforms into a big melee blob when XCOM approaches (or when revealed). Undetectable until it transforms. Big HP, long melee reach. Not in the pre-mission count.

enemy_roster.name: Chryssalid
enemy_roster.signature: Fast melee (Dodge 10-20). All hits POISON; a unit killed by the poison becomes a COCOON that hatches THREE new Chryssalids if not destroyed during gestation. Can BURROW (hide underground, cannot move while burrowed) and ambush. Swarm threat.

enemy_roster.name: Sectopod
enemy_roster.signature: Two-tile-tall robot; occupies a 3x3 footprint (9 tiles), has 3 ACTIONS per turn. High Stance (extra reach/range). Lightning Field = melee-range AoE; Wrath Cannon = devastating line shot. Heavy armor + huge hack defense. Robotic. The X2 apex non-boss. source_quality: HP/armor community-measured (vigaroe via search).

enemy_roster.name: Avatar
enemy_roster.damage: Psi Lance, Teleport-strike, Rift, summon Psi-Zombies
enemy_roster.signature: FINAL BOSS. Self-heals, teleports, clones-of-Codex-style evasion, mass psi (Null Lance line, Psionic Rift, Dimensional Rift). The campaign-ending fight (3 Avatars in the final mission). hp_flag: scales with story/difficulty, no single clean published number.

enemy_roster.name: The Lost (basic)
enemy_roster.signature: Zombie HORDE on ruined-city maps. Individually trivial (2 HP) but ENDLESS - spawn in waves of many. Attack BOTH XCOM and ADVENT. A rifle KILL grants a free 'Lost Headshot' bonus action (chain kills). source_quality: community-measured (vigaroe via search).

enemy_roster.name: The Lost (Dasher)
enemy_roster.signature: Fast Lost variant - mobility 24 (~16 tiles) closes huge gaps in one turn. More HP than basic. source_quality: community-measured.

enemy_roster.name: The Lost (Brute/Howler)
enemy_roster.signature: Rare beefy Lost; slow but high HP, internal name 'Howler' (can call in more Lost). source_quality: community-measured.

enemy_roster.name: ADVENT Purifier
enemy_roster.signature: Flamethrower trooper; sprays fire AoE that ignites cover. EXPLODES on death (area damage). Anti-Lost and anti-clustered-squad. hp_flag: approximate.

enemy_roster.name: ADVENT Priest
enemy_roster.signature: Psi trooper: Mind Control, Stasis (lock a unit in a bubble for a turn), Holy Warrior (buff an ally with shield + reflect). Spawns Spectral Zombies. hp_flag: approximate.

enemy_roster.name: Chosen Assassin
enemy_roster.signature: Stealth boss rival. Goes invisible, closes and SLASHES; can KIDNAP a soldier and carry them off. 1 armor, 5 Dodge. Learns your tactics across the campaign; gets stronger each appearance. Her presence FREEZES the mission timer until she retreats. Permanently killed only at her Stronghold. source_quality: community-measured (vigaroe/Fandom via search).

enemy_roster.name: Chosen Hunter
enemy_roster.signature: Sniper boss rival. Grapples to high ground, picks off soldiers at range; Tracking Shot; can daze/capture. 1 armor, 10 Dodge (hardest to hit). Freezes timer; kidnaps; ramps over campaign. source_quality: community-measured.

enemy_roster.name: Chosen Warlock
enemy_roster.damage: Psi (Spectral Army summon, Mind Control, teleport)
enemy_roster.signature: Psi boss rival - toughest Chosen (2 armor, 30 HP). Summons a Spectral Army (zombie adds), Mind Controls, teleports. Freezes timer; kidnaps; ramps over campaign. source_quality: community-measured.

enemy_ai_behavior.headline: XCOM AI = POD-BASED. Aliens are dormant in pods, patrol-drift toward the squad, and only ACT once a soldier's line-of-sight reveals the pod. On reveal they get a free 'scamper' to cover, then act next turn with aggressive flank/focus-fire logic. Firaxis deliberately UNDER-tunes flank-avoidance so the player can out-position the AI - it is beatable by design.

activation.trigger: An UNCONCEALED XCOM soldier gains line-of-sight to ANY member of a dormant pod. (In X2, an enemy can also activate by gaining LOS to a non-concealed soldier on the enemy turn, or by being flanked.)
activation.on_reveal_scamper: The whole pod plays a reveal beat and each member gets ONE free 'scamper' move toward the nearest cover that protects it from the spotters. This is a one-time repositioning that does NOT cost their upcoming turn. X2 specifically SPREADS the pod out on this move so one grenade/AoE can't wipe it (anti-cheese vs EU's clustered reveals).
activation.scamper_exception: If a soldier is ALREADY flanked or in the open when the pod reveals, members that have a shot SKIP the scamper and FIRE instead (this is the punish for triggering a pod with an exposed soldier).
activation.then: They act normally on the NEXT enemy turn with full offensive AI.
activation.implementable: pod = {units[], patrol_anchor, state:'dormant'}. Each enemy turn while dormant: drift patrol toward squad's last-known centroid by ~1 move. On any soldier gaining LOS to a unit: state='active'; for each member: if it has a valid shot on a flanked/exposed soldier -> shoot; else -> moveToNearestCoverAwayFrom(spotters) as a FREE action. Mark pod active; from next enemy turn run full AI.

alert_states_X2.green: Concealed/unaware. If forced to activate while green (e.g. squad still concealed), pod takes only DEFENSIVE actions (hunker/overwatch), no offense.
alert_states_X2.yellow: Aware via SOUND (gunfire, explosions, a dead ally seen) but not yet LOS-activated. Moves toward the disturbance; may take opportunistic shots; can become a reinforcement next turn.
alert_states_X2.implementable: Track pod.alert in {green,yellow,red}. Noise events (a nearby fight) flip green->yellow within a radius and pull the pod toward the noise. LOS reveal -> red.

per_turn_priority_when_active: 1. KILL SHOT: if any move+shot can KILL a soldier this turn, do it (focus the unit it can finish). AI tries kill shots first.
2. FLANK: else move to a tile that FLANKS a soldier (ignores their cover + crit bonus) and shoot. Will leave cover / take low cover ONLY if that move yields a flank.
3. AoE: if an area ability hits 2+ soldiers, strongly prefer it (especially when no flank exists; sometimes even when one does).
4. BEST SAFE SHOT: else take the highest-hit-% shot from a tile that ALSO keeps the enemy in cover vs the most threats.
5. REPOSITION/HUNKER: if no good shot, move to better cover (un-flankable by one soldier move) and/or hunker/overwatch.
6. INTENTIONAL IMPERFECTION: flank-avoidance is loose - the AI often leaves a flank lane open for the player. Do NOT make it optimal.
enemy_ai_behavior.movement_style: Active enemies generally MOVE + SHOOT (close to a good firing tile, then fire) rather than pure-dash. Melee/rush types (Stun Lancer, Berserker, Chryssalid, Faceless, Archon-frenzied) DASH to close the gap. Ranged types hold cover and trade. Untriggered pods slowly drift toward the squad over several turns.
enemy_ai_behavior.reinforcements: On many (timed) X2 missions ADVENT drops reinforcements from a gunship: a FLARE marks the landing tiles the turn BEFORE they arrive (telegraphed). They land and act the following turn. Implement as a scheduled spawn with a 1-turn warning marker.

per_archetype_rules.basic_ranged (ADVENT Trooper/Officer, Se: Standard priority list. Take cover, shoot best target, flank when free. Officer uses Mark Target on a high-value soldier; Sectoid prefers Mindspin/Reanimate when no clean flank; Muton throws a grenade at 2+ clustered soldiers and Suppresses a flanker.
per_archetype_rules.melee_rusher (Stun Lancer, Berserker, Ch: Each turn DASH toward the nearest reachable soldier; attack if in range. Berserker Bull-Rushes in a straight line THROUGH cover. Chryssalid prioritizes organics it can convert and will burrow to ambush. Faceless stays disguised until a soldier is within ~melee approach, then transforms and strikes. Ignore self-preservation.
per_archetype_rules.flyer (Floater, Heavy Floater, Cyberdisc: Use flight to take HIGH GROUND (aim+def) or reposition over obstacles. Archon: when un-flanked and facing 2+ targets, cast Blazing Pinions (mark AoE tiles, resolve next turn) then reposition; when WOUNDED, Battle Frenzy -> +1 action, dash-melee the nearest soldier. Cyberdisc opens to Death Blossom when 2+ soldiers are adjacent/close.
per_archetype_rules.controller (Viper, Sectoid Commander, Et: Prefer disabling abilities over plain shots. Viper: Tongue Pull a soldier OUT of cover (toward itself), then Bind it next turn (locks both); prioritize an isolated soldier. Sectoid Commander/Ethereal/Priest: Mind Control the strongest soldier or Panic/Stasis a key one; Rift on a low-Will cluster.
per_archetype_rules.teleporter (Codex): Almost never walks - Teleport (no cooldown) to a flanking/safe tile. When facing 2+ soldiers, drop a Psionic Rift on them (disables their weapons, detonates next turn) then teleport away. On taking damage it CLONES (split HP); play both halves.
per_archetype_rules.two_stage_tank (Andromedon): Living form: advance, Cannon the best target, drop Acid Bombs on clusters / to shred cover; tanks hits with 4 armor. On death -> spawn the Shell (own unit, melee, advances and punches).
per_archetype_rules.heavy_boss (Sectopod, Gatekeeper): Slow, stays mid/back, uses 3 actions (Sectopod) to High-Stance + Wrath Cannon a line or Lightning Field a cluster. Gatekeeper opens to beam the best target or Consume/Gateway to reanimate corpses + heal; closes (high def) when threatened.
per_archetype_rules.horde (the Lost): Mindless: every Lost dashes at the nearest living unit (XCOM OR ADVENT) and melees. Spawn in WAVES (many at once), trivial HP. Dasher closes from far. Reward player chain-kills (Lost Headshot bonus action on a rifle kill).
per_archetype_rules.chosen_boss (Assassin/Hunter/Warlock): Recurring rival that INVADES mid-mission. Assassin: stealth-approach + sword + attempt KIDNAP of a low-HP soldier. Hunter: grapple to high ground + long-range sniper + tranq. Warlock: summon a Spectral Army (zombie adds) + Mind Control + teleport. Their presence FREEZES the mission timer. They retreat when low and return stronger later.

clone_recommendation.minimum_viable: Replace the flat 'aggressive' AI with: (1) POD grouping + dormant/active state + LOS reveal + free scamper-to-cover, (2) the 5-step per-turn priority (kill > flank > AoE > best-safe-shot > reposition/hunker), (3) move+shoot for ranged, dash-to-close for melee. That alone makes it FEEL like XCOM.
clone_recommendation.stretch: Add green/yellow/red alert (noise pulls pods), telegraphed reinforcement flares on later/timed missions, and 3-4 special movers (a Viper-style pull, an Archon-style telegraphed AoE, a Codex-style teleport+clone, a Chryssalid-style burrow/convert) to give the roster identity.
clone_recommendation.tuning: Keep flank-avoidance imperfect on purpose. Cap how many pods can be active at once early (1-2) so the player isn't dogpiled; let more activate on bigger/later maps.

campaign_ramp_meta.directly_usable: enemy_count and pod_layout are ready to drive a generator. Algorithm: for mission i, read enemy_count -> instantiate pods from pod_layout -> for each pod pick (size) enemies of the given tier from a tier-bucketed roster -> place pod at a patrol anchor spread across the map_tiles grid -> set pod dormant. tier buckets map to enemy_roster[].tier (1=grunt,2=mid,3=heavy,4=boss).
campaign_ramp_meta.ratio_curve: 1.6x -> 2.0 -> 2.4 -> 2.8 -> 3.2 -> 3.6 -> 4.4x. Always > 1x (aliens always outnumber the squad), escalating like XCOM's early-abduction-to-final-mission curve.
campaign_ramp_meta.vs_xcom_canon: M1-2 ~ EU early abductions (6-10). M3 ~ Terror (12). M4-5 ~ Difficult/UFO (14-16). M6 ~ Alien Base (18, vs canon 21). M7 ~ final swarm (22, vs canon Temple Ship/Battleship 20-26). Counts sit just under EU's late canon to stay fair for a 5-squad with a browser UI.
campaign_ramp_meta.if_owner_wants_even_more: Multiply enemy_count by 1.25-1.5 and raise pods accordingly (cap active pods at 2-3 so it stays playable). LW2 bands (up to 31-34) are the ceiling if you want true swarms - but raise squad size and add AoE tools to match.

difficulty_knobs.headline: XCOM scales difficulty by tuning, in order of impact: (1) enemy COUNT + POD SIZE, (2) enemy HP, (3) enemy AIM/crit, (4) pod composition (tougher species earlier), (5) timers, (6) soldier HP/economy. The clone should expose these as per-difficulty multipliers.

EU2012.source: ufopaedia Alien_Deployment + per-enemy stat tables (canonical). Difficulties: Easy, Normal, Classic, Impossible.
EU2012.enemy_count: Same pod COUNT across most difficulties, but Impossible adds +1 to the rolled abduction difficulty AND removes per-species caps (e.g. 5 Sectopods can appear on a Terror site). Total aliens per mission rise on Classic/Impossible (abduction Difficult = 8 on Easy/Normal/Classic but 10 on Impossible; Very Difficult = 10 -> 12).
EU2012.enemy_hp: Most aliens gain HP on Classic/Impossible (Sectoid 3->4, Thin Man 4->6, Floater 4->6, Muton 10->10, Heavy Floater 14->16, Cyberdisc 16->20, Mechtoid 22->24, Muton Elite 14->18, Ethereal 20->25, Berserker 20->25). Sectopod flat 30.
EU2012.enemy_aim: Aim rises on Classic/Impossible (Sectoid 65->75, Muton 70->80, Cyberdisc 70->80, Muton Elite 80->90/100, Sectopod 80->90).
EU2012.player_side: Lower difficulty = more soldier HP/aim leeway, cheaper research, slower panic. (EU base game is largely UNTIMED regardless of difficulty.)

XCOM2.source: Fandom Game_difficulty_(XCOM2) summary (community-measured). Difficulties: Rookie, Veteran, Commander, Legend.
XCOM2.pod_size: The big lever. Veteran = mostly 2 enemies/pod. Commander/Legend = mostly 3/pod. (Force Level also raises pod size as the campaign advances.)
XCOM2.enemy_hp: Enemies gain HP each step (see roster Rookie/Vet/Cmd/Legend columns: e.g. Sectoid 7/8/8/10, Muton 8/8/9/11, Archon 12/18/20/24, Gatekeeper 20/20/25/30, Andromedon 12/15/18/21). Some gain ARMOR on Commander+.
XCOM2.enemy_aim_crit: Aim/crit rise (e.g. ADVENT Officer gains innate +10 crit on Commander/Legend; many aim bumps Rookie->Veteran).
XCOM2.timers: Mission turn timers are TIGHTER on higher difficulty / Force Level (Guerrilla Ops ~6-8 turns, Council ~12). WOTC option can DOUBLE all timers.
XCOM2.force_level: FL 1->20 drives WHICH enemies appear and how big pods are over the campaign (the real progression engine; see enemy_progression). Beyond FL20, no further composition change.
XCOM2.player_side: Higher difficulty = less soldier HP, slower will recovery, harsher economy, faster Avatar doom clock.

expose_per_difficulty.enemy_count_mult: Easy 0.8 / Normal 1.0 / Hard 1.2 (apply to campaign_ramp enemy_count, then re-pod).
expose_per_difficulty.pod_size_target: Easy 2 / Normal 3 / Hard 3 (Hard also raises max active pods).
expose_per_difficulty.enemy_hp_mult: Easy 0.85 / Normal 1.0 / Hard 1.2 (or use the 4-column native stats directly).
expose_per_difficulty.enemy_aim_add: Easy -10 / Normal 0 / Hard +10 (on the 0-100 aim before /100).
expose_per_difficulty.timer: Easy = none/long / Normal = generous / Hard = XCOM-tight (expose per-mission turn_limit, null=untimed).
expose_per_difficulty.active_pod_cap: Easy 1 / Normal 2 / Hard 3 (how many pods may be in 'active' state simultaneously).

clone_recommendation.ordering: Tune COUNT/POD-SIZE first (biggest felt difference), then HP, then aim/crit, then timers. Do NOT just inflate aim - XCOM's difficulty is mostly 'more, tankier enemies in bigger pods', which is exactly what the owner is asking for.
